title: Haiya
text:
The world ended
People continued. Seasons turn.
I do karate.

title: Short and loud
text:
There once was a solarpunk band
On a stage in a fest and they found
Their speakers were loud
It impressed the crowd
Till their battery discharged with a bang!
Patrick Barry

title: Permaquilture
text:
The orchard creaks beneath the storm
Beneath my blankets I am warm
The cobots charge inside the barn
As the storm washes over our farm
Patrick Barry

title: Solarpunk Poetry Book
text:
It’s an idea I can’t shake. I love poetry, but I’m pretty miserable at the moment. I can’t handle the angst of Young poets on climate change - the power of being a young writer.
So, be the change you want.
I want to put together a set of light-hearted poetry about places and characters (like Pam Ayres “Who are you calling vermin”), but set in a recognisable solarpunk world. Poems that might be called “Overheard at the Library”, “Ballad of Bike Bridge”, “The Agrivoltician’s Holiday”, “Lawnmower’s Reincarnation”, etc.

title: Solarpunk Poetry Book
text:
Rough Plan
Small paper book, 34 lines to a page.
Submissions close end of Jan 2027.
Send to cromlyngames@gmail.com with subject: “solarpunk poetry book submission”.
Plan A is all typeset and made available for download, local print on demand (as we have done for Fully Automated RPG). Plan B is using LaTeX to set out as a foldable, bindable zine, and personally doing a limited print run for participants (postage from UK is going to suck).

title: Solarpunk Poetry Book
text:
What I need

Share this to likely people; there is a world out there, and a small target!
If submitting, somewhere between 3-9 English-language poems, ideally 6 with varied topics. This is to get variety so many different people can be accepted.
Ideally no poem longer than 100 lines, be kind to your editor.
Poems rated PG at worst. I want to be able to give a copy of this to my 12 year old niece.
If submitting, include a very short blurb. This may or may not be your real name, I don’t really care.
Please include explicit permission for me to share your email address with other editors (UK GDPR).
If you are interested/willing to workshop poems with other entrants, please state so. I’d like to be able to link some like-minded people up together. This is simialr to the fantastic guides and support on https://www.reddit.com/r/OCPoetry/ with
If not submitting, but interested in getting a copy at the end, shoot me an email saying so.

title: A Gardener Needs
text:
A Gardener needs
They need plants and robots
and spades and lasers
to grow… to grow…
weeds! and flowers
and fruit and peanuts
and vines and gourds
and cabbage and mint
Ah Kinder, but most
of all they need
Patience
And a friend who likes jam.



What do they need Gran?
Granny! Granny!
she said a naughty word!
What do they need Gran?



I know! I know!



by
Patrick Barry

title: Slightly Foxed
text:
I saw your camdem skirt-
swirl as you turned-
for more books from-
your rolling cart.
One night you’d smiled-
and said you’d learned-
that reshelving done-
you’d touched every book-
in the building.
A quiet pride burned-
at order spun-
open to all.
Patrick Barry

title: Makerspace
text:
Valentino’s mad at Jonny.
Jonny sliced his finger
Now Valentino’s got to
update the accident book.
Sean has his head down
in the corner
The soldering iron
cools
Pete and Jenny hunch over a laptop
Looks like a proposal
Andre snorts loudly. Rob rubs oil into his plane sole.
They are arguing about construction of identity again
Or sausages.
The kettle finishes boiling.
I distribute teas and go to watch my sculpture.
The shape hasn’t quite fallen out of its shape yet.
Patrick Barry
